I finished my master's at KUT last year and have been at Aurinko Avionics since January working on beamforming for weather radar receivers, but I want to explain why I am already looking at Kaikuvaara and why I think this makes sense despite the short tenure.

The system acquired 16 channels of biopotential data on a STM32H7 microcontroller, ran real-time IIR notch filtering and baseline wander removal, and streamed processed data over USB to a host PC for recording. I wrote the firmware in C, handled the DMA configuration and interrupt priorities, and validated the signal chain against a calibrated reference. It was a side project in the sense that it was not part of my thesis, but it was a full real-time system on constrained hardware that worked and that the biomedical group continued to use after I graduated. I mention it because it demonstrates that I can design and deliver a working signal pipeline on a microcontroller platform — different domain, different hardware, same discipline.

I am early in my career and this is a senior role, which I understand. But the technical foundation is there — array processing, RF measurement, production Python — and I am looking for the place where I can build depth. I think Kaikuvaara is that place.
